newsitem.title: USA: Odwalla, Starbucks sued in food poisoning.
newsitem.headline: Odwalla, Starbucks sued in food poisoning.

text.p: The first lawsuit has been filed stemming from an outbreak of bacterial poisoning linked to Odwalla Inc apple juice, a lawyer said Friday.

The lawsuit against Odwalla and retailer Starbucks Corp was filed in Seattle's King County Superior Court on behalf of a six-year-old boy who was hospitalized and required abdominal surgery after being infected by a dangerous strain of E. coli bacteria.
The boy was one of more than 40 people in Colorado, California, Washington and British Columbia sickened in the past several weeks by bacteria linked to tainted apple juice.

Odwalla has recalled all products containing apple juice as well as carrot juice, which is made on the same production line, and has said it will pay medical expenses for anyone sickened by its drinks.
Odwalla officials could not be reached for immediate comment, and a Starbucks spokeswoman said the coffee-bar chain had not been served with the lawsuit.

Kelly Corr, the lawyer for the boy, said the lawsuit sought unspecified compensation for loss of wages and pain and suffering. The suit also seeks punitive damages on the theory that Starbucks and Odwalla should have known that unpasteurized apple juice posed a risk.
He pointed to medical journal reports as early as 1993 that linked apple cider to E. coli.
"It seems to me at the point they should have done something," Corr said.
Corr said he was "guardedly optimistic" about the boy's health but declined to give details.
